name: Pan-Fried Tilapia with Potato, Snap Pea & Mint Salad

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 medium red potatoes
3 (227 g) pkg sugar snap peas
1 ½ lemon
1 ½ small pkg fresh mint

instructions.primary_message: Quarter the potatoes lengthwise (into wedges) and transfer to a medium saucepan. Cover with hot water (from the tap) by about 2 ½ cm and bring to a boil over high heat.
Grate the zest from the lemons, then juice the lemons; add both to a large bowl (that will hold the salad).
To the salad bowl, add yogurt, olive oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk together.
instructions.secondary_message:
¾ cup plain Greek yogurt
3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
3 tsp Dijon mustard
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, cook the potato pieces until they are tender when pierced with a knife or fork, 10 to 15 minutes, making sure not to overcook. Drain in a colander.
Halve the sugar snap peas at an angle; add to the salad bowl.
Pick the mint leaves off the stems; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add to the salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the shallots; peel and finely dice the shallots. Add to the salad bowl.
Add olive oil to a nonstick skillet and preheat over medium heat.
instructions.secondary_message: 1 ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.primary_message: Pat the tilapia dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg tilapia fillet
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the skillet is hot, add the tilapia; cook until it is cooked through and golden brown, 2 to 4 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Cut the potato quarters crosswise into 6-mm-thick pieces; add to the salad bowl. Gently toss the salad until well coated with the dressing.
To serve, divide the tilapia and salad between plates. Enjoy!
